record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Can current Everpresent Lambda models, or slightly modified versions of them, quantitatively alleviate both the Hubble tension in measurements of H0 and the S8 tension in measurements of matter clustering, without the common failure mode in which resolving one correlated tension worsens the other?

evidence.quote: The Hubble tension is the name given to a clash in recent measurements of the Hubble parameter H0, with disagreements between supernova (together with Cepheid stars and tip of the red giant branch) data and observations from the cosmic microwave background.
S8 ≡ σ8√Ωm/0.3 is the parameter used to quantify this tension, where Ωm is the fraction of the total energy density belonging to matter.
At present, there are only qualitative indications that Everpresent Λ possesses some of the features that are believed to be key to resolving the Hubble and S8 tensions.

Carrying out a dedicated and quantitative study of how much the current Everpresent Λ models (or slightly modified versions of them) can alleviate these tensions is one of the most important directions of future work on Everpresent Λ.

The S8 and Hubble tensions are correlated tensions, namely, many proposed models that alleviate one tension tend to worsen the other. Therefore it would be very interesting to see if Everpresent Λ can alleviate both at the same time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker cosmology, let H(z) denote the Hubble parameter as a function of redshift z, with present value H_0 = H(0). Let Ω_m denote the present-day matter density parameter and let σ_8 denote the rms linear matter density fluctuation on a comoving scale of 8 h^{-1} Mpc. Define the clustering parameter
   S_8 := σ_8 · sqrt(Ω_m / 0.3).
Two well-known observational tensions in the standard ΛCDM cosmology are:
 (i) the "Hubble tension": values of H_0 inferred from cosmic-microwave-background data assuming ΛCDM are systematically lower than values measured from low-redshift distance-ladder probes (e.g. Cepheids/SNIa, TRGB);
 (ii) the "S_8 tension": the value of S_8 inferred from cosmic-microwave-background data is systematically higher than values measured from weak-lensing and large-scale-structure surveys.

Consider a class of "Everpresent Λ" cosmological models in which the cosmological term Λ(t) is not constant but is a stochastic function of cosmic time whose mean value is statistically tied to the inverse spacetime volume to the past, and whose fluctuations may take either sign. Concretely, one models Λ as a random variable satisfying Λ V ~ O(1) (with V the spacetime four-volume to the past of the relevant epoch) with Poisson-type fluctuations of variance of order 1/V, coupled to the standard Friedmann equations either directly or via a modification preserving general covariance and energy-momentum conservation up to stochastic source terms.

Problem. Construct, within the class of Everpresent Λ models (or a "slight" modification thereof, in which one keeps the defining stochastic Λ V ~ O(1) feature but allows a finite-parameter alteration of the dynamics or initial conditions), a model with the following properties:
 (a) When fit jointly to current cosmic-microwave-background, baryon-acoustic-oscillation, Type Ia supernova, and weak-lensing/large-scale-structure data, the model yields posterior 1-D marginals for H_0 and S_8 each consistent with the corresponding low-redshift direct measurement at the ≲ 2σ level;
 (b) The improvement in H_0 is not obtained at the cost of worsening the fit to S_8, and vice versa (i.e., the resolution evades the standard correlated trade-off in which decreasing the sound horizon to raise H_0 raises S_8);
 (c) The overall goodness-of-fit to the combined data is at least as good as ΛCDM.

Either exhibit such a model and quantify the residual tensions, or prove that no such model exists within this class.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on "Aspects of Everpresent Λ" (Parts I and II) establish the model's fluctuating-Λ framework and perform cosmological tests, but only provide qualitative indications that Everpresent Λ has features potentially relevant to the Hubble and S_8 tensions. No published study to date demonstrates that current or slightly modified Everpresent Λ models quantitatively resolve both tensions simultaneously, and the question is explicitly identified as an important direction of future work.

status_evidence.title: Aspects of Everpresent Λ (II): Cosmological Tests of Current Models
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological tests of current Everpresent Λ models are presented; the work does not claim a quantitative resolution of both H_0 and S_8 tensions.
status_evidence.claim: Existing tests of current Everpresent Λ models do not establish a joint quantitative resolution of the Hubble and S_8 tensions.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological Tests of Everpresent Λ
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier cosmological tests of Everpresent Λ focus on basic compatibility with data rather than the H_0/S_8 tensions.
status_evidence.claim: Prior literature treats Everpresent Λ only qualitatively in relation to the tensions.
